column1: # The benchmark suite: one line per benchmark, read by run-bench.sh (sweep and
# --check-scenarios). Fields, separated by whitespace:
#   lib          library under test; its rule file is /tmp/.chaos-<lib>.conf and its binary
#                benchmark/build/bench_<lib>
#   passthrough  benchmark name of the arm run with the library but an empty rule file
#   prefix       <prefix>_match_no_fire and <prefix>_errno are the other two arms
#   iters        measured iterations, or - for BENCH_ITERS; caps the slow calls
#   empty        scenario of the passthrough arm (an empty rule file)
#   stem         <stem>-match-no-fire.conf and <stem>-errno.conf; the match-no-fire file is
#                the errno file with probability 0, so both select the same calls
#   mode         full (sweep only with --full), smoke (also with --smoke), or linux (full,
#                and skipped when the binary does not register the benchmark)
#   krev         kernel revision: bump when the benchmark's iteration body or setup changes
#                what it measures (all three arms)
#   srev         scenario revision: bump when <stem>-*.conf changes what is matched or
#                injected (match-no-fire and errno arms)
# run-bench.sh copies this file into every report directory, so the release envelopes carry
# it. The release-over-release gate compares a benchmark only when its revision is the same in
# both releases; a changed one is listed as re-baselined for one release and not gated. A
# report directory without the file (2.0.0 and earlier) counts as revision 1 throughout.
# Every benchmark is also run without LD_PRELOAD (tag "baseline") before each arm.
# Benchmark names are the comparison key across releases: renaming one drops it from the
# release-over-release gate for one release.
# lib    passthrough                  prefix          iters  empty               stem                 mode   krev  srev
time     clock_gettime_baseline       clock_gettime   -      empty.conf          clock_gettime        smoke  1     2
